entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Gaius Fannius was a Roman Republican politician of the second century BCE who reached the consulship (122 BCE) amid the Gracchan crisis. Associated with the circle of Scipio Aemilianus yet navigating popularis pressures, he appears in sources as an orator and statesman in the decade when agrarian and judicial reforms polarised the elite.

Fannius’s consulship year was charged: conflict over Gracchan measures and allied Italian questions strained mos maiorum politics. Later rhetorical tradition remembered speeches linked to his name, feeding the Roman oratorical canon.

He exemplifies the mid-republican nobilis caught between reformist tribunes and conservative senatorial reaction on the eve of Rome’s longer revolution.
